_comment: ARCH-020 seed: the vehicle maintenance record as assembled by Spool on
2026-09-01 from FIVE independent sources -- Carfax export (58 records), two
Maas Automotive repair orders, two Peter's Highline invoices, photo EXIF, and
this project's own telemetry in obd2db.
This file is the version-controlled copy. Before it existed the record lived
ONLY as Markdown on the fleet share, which was confirmed on 2026-09-01 to have
no snapshots and no undo of any kind (ext4 on RAID 5; Synology snapshots need
Btrfs). In S41 a script truncated a 22,588-byte file to 0 bytes and the only
surviving copy was the one that lived in the database.
PROVENANCE IS PER FIELD, NOT PER ROW. The 2026-08-22 oil change carries a
CIO-declared odometer FACT, a recollected brand, and an ABSENT viscosity in one
row. A single row-level confidence would force downgrading the odometer or
upgrading the brand -- both are lies.
DATE PRECISION IS STATED, NEVER IMPLIED. event_date is a sortable ANCHOR. Where
precision is 'month' or 'range' the anchor's day is an artefact of storage and
MUST NOT be quoted as the event date -- use formatEventDate().

DATE CERTAINTY (CIO 2026-09-02) is ORTHOGONAL to precision. Precision says how fine-grained the date is; certainty says whether a source RECORDED it or somebody ESTIMATED it. Seq 3 stores 1999-04-01 for the second of three services in a Carfax window -- that date is an INTERPOLATION invented to sort the row, and before this column nothing distinguished it from 2008-05-08, which a dealer actually wrote down.

events.provenance: PER-FIELD, and this row is why the rule exists. odometer 78,907 = CIO-DECLARED FACT (exact). Oil brand = RECOLLECTION ('I believe'). Viscosity = ABSENT, not recorded by anyone. One row-level confidence column would force downgrading the odometer or upgrading the brand; both would be false.
events.notes: Odometer anchor for the whole record. A transposed 78,097 was filed once and corrected -- an anchor error is a permanent offset on every derived mileage forever, with no sensor able to catch it.

events.provenance: date: CIO-declared appointment, forward-dated at time of landing (2026-09-01). NOT a completed event: this row records that the appointment exists. Update work_performed, odometer and odometer_source from the invoice afterwards.
events.notes: Ask about SPARK PLUGS while there -- seq 48 is the only item in the record with no date at all, and its heat range and gap matter before any boost work.

events.provenance: date: OWNER-REPORTED as 'within the last ~4 years' -- an OWNER-ESTIMATED four-year window, not a source-recorded date. This is what makes it different in kind from every other row: the Carfax windows (seq 2-4, 8-9, 21-22, 35-36) are recorded by a source; this one is a recollection. Brand, heat range and gap are ALL UNKNOWN.
events.notes: NUMBERED 48 DELIBERATELY. Spool's canonical count is '47 DATED events' and this item is explicitly 'the only maintenance item with no date at all', so it sits outside that numbering rather than renumbering his record. It is still a real event that really happened, so it belongs in the log -- dropping it would lose the fact that the work was done. The only maintenance item whose SPECIFICATION (heat range, gap) matters before boost.

schedule.notes: INFERRED, NOT CONFIRMED. The only candidate in 28 years is seq 17, a 2008 '60,000 MILE SERVICE' that names no belt; no timing-belt line item appears in ANY of four independent sources. Miles are fine (~10k since 2008); TIME is 3.7x over (18.3 years against a 5-year interval) on an INTERFERENCE engine. This row is the reason last_done_confidence exists: without it the belt reads as serviced in 2008. Resolve before the ECMLink base tune or any boost work.
Last done 2026-08-22 at 78,907 mi (Fuller Car Wash). At ~500 mi/yr the calendar interval is the only one that will ever fire.
